purpose: WELL-136 bounded development password-reset journey. Identity owns proof issuance and credential replacement; Content owns exact eligible copy; Communications owns durable email obligation and provider attempt. No production activation or participant release authority.

implementation_revision.semantics: Committed WELL-136 application and regression-test source checkpoint. This map describes bounded development behavior and does not certify independent review, complete local gates, CI, FP-001 completion or release.

collaborating_domains.ownership: Persists source-bound MessageIntent and delivery admission/attempt; does not own proof, bearer, Account eligibility or credential outcome.

collaborating_domains.ownership: Revalidates eligible exact email content and provides pinned EN/AF browser wording for this development journey.

Private Identity-owned proof actions called within PasswordReset transactions.

Executor persists admission and provider observations through private owner actions.

caller_constraints: Development proof environment only; requires current historical P8-12 Content eligibility, independently of Phase-9 applicability. Does not create Account or authenticate.

returns: :ok neutral response, including unsupported or ineligible contexts.

side_effects: Atomically consumes proof, replaces password, revokes sessions/devices, invalidates registration operations and records security obligation.

caller_constraints: Trusted Communications executor only; bearer is transient and is not persisted in Communications.

side_effects: Binds current eligible Content, platform provenance and render digest; persists durable intent.

request_flow.summary: Controller admits routes only in dev/test with verification fixtures and pinned browser-copy artifacts. Trusted ordinary-entry configuration selects WELL-136 before the legacy fixture flag; unavailable ordinary entry never falls back to P8-12. Request rendering and submission check Content eligibility for that selected scope, and the controller passes the context explicitly to Identity.
Identity canonicalizes email and locale, accepts only an existing eligible Account, then locks Account and performs idempotent request handling within an Ash transaction.

Under the Account lock, a new request supersedes current proofs and creates a 15-minute proof with fixed claims, Account binding, locale and request UUID. The selected server context fixes the email render schema. Communications checks current eligibility for that schema and establishes the content-bound intent in the same Identity transaction. Ineligible Content rolls back supersession, proof creation and intent together.

Executor checks the source, current Content and render eligibility, then commits attempt admission before it invokes the configured deterministic test provider outside authoritative transactions. Communications owns the unknown provider submission and reconciliation state; this never proves Identity reset completion.

GET/HEAD only render the explicit form. CSRF-protected POST invokes Identity reset. Identity locks Account/proof, verifies current claims, rejects current password, consumes proof and writes credential/security consequences atomically.

guards: Valid EN/AF locale, valid operation UUID, canonical email, existing verified/open/active/normal Account, and successful bounded request transaction.
Current Content eligibility for the explicitly selected development scope, validated by Communications within the issuance transaction.
side_effects: Issue a proof with a 15-minute expiry and establish a content-bound email intent in the same transaction.

guards: A new eligible request for the Account with a different request operation UUID.
side_effects: Supersede prior proof before issuing replacement in the transaction.

guards: Explicit valid, unexpired, current proof; Account binding matches; password differs from current password; confirmation operation UUID is valid.
side_effects: Consume proof and atomically perform password/security consequences.

guards: Proof expires or Identity revokes it.
side_effects: Proof cannot authorize reset. Expiry is timestamp-based; revocation is an Identity token outcome.

guards: Retry presents the same stored confirmation operation UUID.
side_effects: Return :already_reset without applying the retry password.

security_invariants.summary: Request response is neutral and bounded; invalid, unknown, ineligible, timeout and internal failure do not disclose Account existence.
Only dev/test with explicit verification fixture and current eligible exact EN/AF copy can use this journey. Browser copy has no locale fallback.
Proof is purpose-bound, short-lived, single-use, bound to current Account security state and signing key; no direct token creation occurs during delivery.
No automatic login or Session issuance follows reset; existing sessions and trusted devices are revoked.
No production provider or participant release authority is added; delivery uses the deterministic test provider.

concurrency.summary: Account row lock serializes issuance, supersession and consumption; proof row lock protects explicit consumption; transaction spans Account, Token, Session, DeviceAssurance, RegistrationOperation and EvidenceObligation.
Unique Token indexes on account_id for current reset proof, reset_consumption_id and reset_request_id provide durable proof and operation uniqueness alongside Account locking.

idempotency_retry.summary: Same request operation UUID finds the prior Token and performs no second issuance or context retargeting. A new eligible request operation supersedes extant proof only if its selected Content scope remains eligible.
Same confirmation UUID on consumed proof returns prior :already_reset without reapplying password. A different operation against consumed proof fails closed.
Request timeout cancels bounded worker; transaction rollback protects interrupted writes. If commit wins cancellation, same operation retry is harmless.
Reset transaction errors that cannot confirm commit return :reset_uncertain; do not report confirmed failure or retry side effects automatically.

failure_recovery.summary: Missing, withdrawn or corrupt Phase-9 applicability does not disable historical P8-12 issuance or delivery when its own approval remains valid. An explicit WELL-136 request still fails closed, rolling back attempted historical proof supersession. Historical delivery separately fails closed on withdrawal of its own approval.
Any failed write in reset transaction rolls back proof consumption, credential replacement, revocations and security evidence together.
Exceptions/uncertain transaction results map to reset_uncertain; invalid proof and validation failure map to reset_unavailable.
Delivery invocation uncertainty belongs to Communications provider reconciliation; delivery evidence never proves reset completion.

Migration down restores the legacy-only message_intents schema check. It will fail while any row has render_schema password-reset-well136-v1. The owner must reconcile this rollback hazard under an authorized procedure; the map prescribes no deletion or transformation.

safe_extensions.summary: Use Identity.request_password_reset/3 only for historical P8-12 scope; ordinary entry uses request_password_reset/4 with explicit :well136. Preserve Identity.reset_password/3, Account/proof lock order and atomic consequences.

Use Communications.establish_password_reset/1 and executor owner checks for delivery changes. Preserve both fresh historical password-reset-v1 issuance and queued historical delivery independently of WELL-136 applicability.
Use Content PasswordResetMessage and PasswordResetBrowserCopy eligibility APIs; do not duplicate or reconstruct approved copy.

reuse.summary: Reuse Identity Token and Account as proof and credential authority; no parallel reset table or proof store.
Reuse Communications MessageIntent and DeliveryAttempt with source-bound eligibility and deterministic test provider.
Reuse exact Content owner artifacts and browser copy fixture with digest checks.

prohibited_shortcuts.summary: Do not expose the flow outside gated dev/test environments or activate a production provider.
Do not consume proof on GET/HEAD, bypass CSRF on confirmation, or create a Session after reset.
Do not store the bearer in MessageIntent or bypass Identity current-proof validation during delivery.
